thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: P1001 fired for GPU pool 'west2a-rt-1' — metric: gpu.memory.used_percent > 92% for 3m. Severity: high. Rule: kvcache_memory_frag -> auto-evict attempted but rate-limited.

pagerduty: Incident P1001 created. Services: gpu-serving-west2a. Escalation level: on-call primary (Aisha).

Aisha: acked on PagerDuty. jumping in now. pinging @Diego for quick pool telemetry.

Diego: on it, pulling metrics. seeing steady mem usage 85-95% with frequent small alloc failures in logs. kvcache evict rate at cap, eviction latency spiking ~300ms.

Ravi: any customer-facing errors? I see increased 429s on a single tenant in west2a-rt-1 in the last 5m. link: https://graf.redwood/alerts/P1001/streams

Aisha: confirmed - customer 'acme-retail' latency and token truncation on a few requests, support flagged 2 incidents. Notify support?

Diego: logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T14:07:34Z cuda: alloc 1024MB failed: out_of_memory
2026-03-15T14:07:34Z kvcache: prefetch miss; fallback to host
2026-03-15T14:07:35Z infer: request_id=abc123 err=OOM retry=1
2026-03-15T14:07:36Z kvcache: eviction call failed: rate_limit
```
Aisha: action plan from oncall playbook -> try temporary pool drain and reroute traffic to compatible pool (west2b-rt-2) to relieve pressure, then increase eviction rate cap and force-gc kvcache. Would that be safe?

Diego: safe if capacity available. west2b-rt-2 currently at 60% mem; can take some burst. I'll prepare reroute rule.

Ravi: explaining to support: "We're seeing GPU memory fragmentation leading to OOMs and falling back to host memory for some requests; we're actively rerouting traffic to reduce tail latency. Expect reduced errors in ~5-10m."

Aisha: executing reroute now: `redwood route update --from pool:west2a-rt-1 --to pool:west2b-rt-2 --pct 80 --reason "mitigation: gpu mem pressure"`

ops-runbook-bot: Command executed by Aisha @ 2026-03-15T14:09:52Z: route update queued, change-id=chg_20260315_001. See runbook: https://runbooks/redwood/gpu-memory-pressure

Diego: monitoring... initial drop in west2a load ~65% within 30s. eviction latency back down to 40ms.

Ravi: support updated; customer impact reduced but still seeing a few retries. collecting sample request IDs for postmortem.

Aisha: temporarily bumping kvcache eviction throttle: `kvcachectl set-evict-cap --pool west2a-rt-1 --value 2.0x` then forcing a GC: `kvcachectl gc --pool west2a-rt-1 --mode aggressive`

ops-runbook-bot: Evict-cap change queued, gc job started (job id gc_5321098765_1).

Diego: after GC: freeable memory increased ~1.2GB, alloc failures stop. No new OOM logs in last 90s.

Aisha: lowering reroute to 20% to keep some load on west2a for graceful decommissioning. `redwood route update --from pool:west2a-rt-1 --to pool:west2b-rt-2 --pct 20`

Ravi: collecting timeline for incident notes: root cause likely kvcache fragmentation + eviction rate cap too conservative under sudden prefetch pattern. Need follow-ups: (1) increase default eviction cap for hot pools, (2) add a kvcache fragmentation alert earlier, (3) perf test prefetch workloads.

Diego: agree. I'll run a diagnostic tool for kvcache fragmentation and paste results into postmortem.

Aisha: handing off to Diego for monitoring and postmortem. I'll go back on next rotation. If anything regresses ping me.

pagerduty: Acknowledgement recorded. Escalation paused.

Diego: will keep watch for 30m then close.

Ravi: adding customer follow-up item and draft message for support to send to acme-retail.

Aisha: closing notes for now: mitigation succeeded, errors dropped from ~12/min to <1/min. Impact window: 14:06 - 14:12 UTC. root cause hypothesis: kvcache fragmentation + rate-limit on evictions under rapid prefetch. Next steps: postmortem, runbook update, default eviction cap bump, add early-warning metric for fragmentation.

ops-runbook-bot: Incident P1001 closed by Aisha @ 2026-03-15T14:22:25Z. Close reason: mitigated, traffic restored.

Diego: postmortem draft will be in #incidents within 24h.

Ravi: thanks all, nice quick coordination :thumbsup:
